items.title: PREVENT post hoc: preventive PCI benefit confined to NIRS-defined lipid-rich plaques
items.summary: Circulation post hoc analysis of PREVENT (598 patients, 632 non-flow-limiting lesions with plaque burden >70% and MLA <4 mm² on IVUS plus NIRS): preventive PCI was associated with fewer primary-outcome events only in lipid-rich plaques (7% vs 18%), with no benefit in non-lipid-rich plaques despite similar anatomy.
bullets: Post hoc analysis of the PREVENT RCT (1,606 patients; South Korea, Japan, Taiwan, New Zealand): 598 patients, 632 lesions with plaque burden >70% and minimal lumen area <4 mm² on IVUS that also had NIRS.
Lipid-rich plaque (LRP) was prespecified as maxLCBI4mm >315; present in 223 patients (37%). Median follow-up 5.6 years.
Primary outcome (cardiac death, target-vessel MI, ischaemia-driven TVR or hospitalisation for unstable/progressive angina) was more frequent with LRP than without (13% vs 5%; HR 2.08, p=0.039).
With LRP, preventive PCI vs optimal medical therapy alone: 7% vs 18% (adjusted HR 0.23, p<0.001). Without LRP: 6% vs 4% (adjusted HR 1.00); P interaction <0.001.
Hypothesis-generating (post hoc): plaque composition may matter beyond burden and lumen size; prospective NIRS-guided preventive PCI trials are needed before routine use.

items.title: AI-enhanced auscultation detects LVEF ≤40% with AUROC 0.90 on external validation (NEJM AI)
items.summary: Prospective multicentre Japanese study (NEJM AI, Oct 15): an AI model analysing digital-stethoscope recordings from four auscultation sites detected LV dysfunction (LVEF ≤40%) with AUROC 0.904 in external validation and beat cardiologist consensus in a reader substudy. Proposed as a pre-echo triage tool, not yet for screening.
bullets: Adults referred for clinically indicated echo had digital auscultation at four standard sites, recorded with a simultaneous single-lead ECG; LV dysfunction was defined as LVEF ≤40% on same-time echo.
Training cohort 2,359 patients (8.9% reduced LVEF); external validation in 964 patients from an independent multicentre registry (7.6% reduced LVEF).
External validation: AUROC 0.904, sensitivity 86.3%, specificity 74.2%; outperformed ECG-only and clinical models (including BNP); a simplified two-site model kept AUROC 0.903.
In a 100-patient reader substudy, AI accuracy was 82% vs 62% for consensus of seven cardiologists (P=0.004).

Limitations: studied in patients already referred for echo (not a general screening population) and industry-sponsored (AMI Inc.; four authors are AMI employees); authors say further validation is needed before broader screening use.
